summary.note: Audit of eight merged pull requests (#484, #497, #530, #538, #544, #547, #531, #535) against github.com/tailscale/tailscale at the ledger's pin v1.102.4 (bbcd7d1fc2054b9189ebc1531acf74bd880ca0c8), cloned shallow at that tag. #497 and #531 were each listed twice for review; each gets one row. Severity: major = observable behaviour differs; minor = wording, framing or order differs.

auditedPrs.notes: Squash 84f399d. The sentence move is real: Go's text now sits whole on line 1 with the path moved below it. Read against cmd/tailscaled/tailscaled.go at the pin. The guard, the empty-path carve-out, the check order (after the debug subcommand, before --cleanup) and exit status 1 all match Go. Two gaps remain. First, line 1 is still not Go's line: it carries an error: prefix, a trailing full stop and fork text in the %s slot, then several paragraphs follow. Second, the flag is refused even on BIRD-capable platforms, where Go wires BIRD up. That one is engine-side. The doc comment and commit cite upstream ref 53a0d659 rather than the ledger pin; the Go code is the same at the pin.

Squash 4dce9c2. One row covers both commits in the squash: the self_change port and the follow-up doc that names the engine gap. Read against Notify.SelfChange in ipn/backend.go and against setControlClientStatusLocked and the NotifyInitialNetMap front-load in ipn/ipnlocal/local.go at the pin. What matches: self_change rides every netmap frame, it is front-loaded under initial_netmap, it has no mask bit of its own, it is nil when no self node exists, and it is never diffed. What does not: a self-only netmap change sends no frame (engine-side, ask #46), and the payload is a five-field projection where Go sends the whole tailcfg.Node.

Squash a787db8. The write path now matches Go: begin_set judges the prospective prefs (current prefs plus edits), so set and check-prefs agree, as editPrefsLocked does upstream. The auto-update rule now runs before the route rule. Divergences: a config-file opt-in hard-fails the config load, where Go's initPrefsFromConfig/setConfigLocked apply it without checkPrefsLocked. The PR discloses this as deliberate. The refusal text extends Go's one sentence. The check chain still runs exit-node rules before SSH, where Go runs SSH before exit-node.

Squash a38687b. The daemon-side string now equals Go's tag: %q: <CheckTag reason> for all four CheckTag clauses, with the completed tag quoted and the first offender reported. Read against cmd/tailscale/cli/up.go prefsFromUpArgs and tailcfg/tailcfg.go CheckTag at the pin. The commit calls the refusal byte-identical to Go's, but that holds for the daemon string only. What an operator sees differs: there is an error: prefix on tnet up, and a JSON object under --json, where Go's fatalf prints the bare line to stderr.

Squash a8b5fbf. All four refusals the PR names now print bare with exit 1, in Go's words and order relative to each other. Read against runServeCombined in cmd/tailscale/cli/serve_v2.go and main in cmd/tailscale/tailscale.go at the pin. The two --service refusals in the same function still print anyhow's context chain. The PR raises this as a question; it does not fix it. The tun-mode refusal is also decided before the daemon is asked, while Go reaches it only after GetServeConfig, the status fetch and the tagged-node check.

divergences: only after the web-client pref round-trip
auditedPrs.notes: Squash c872cca. Fixes the reported bug: every listener run, --readonly included, now ends an interrupt at exit 0, and the pref restore is gated on Go's !cgi && startedManagementClient. Read against runWeb in cmd/tailscale/cli/web.go at the pin. The interrupt arm is installed only after the web-client pref round-trip, where Go arms it as runWeb's first statement. A CGI serve failure also exits 1 here; Go logs it and returns nil.

Squash 3977ad9. One row covers both beads on this PR. Read against Policy.reloadNow in util/syspolicy/rsop/resultant_policy.go and the JSON store in util/syspolicy/source/json_policy_store.go at the pin. Policy frames are now sent only when the items change, and the snapshot is swapped before watchers are woken. Upstream's JSON store also reads its file once, so Go's forced reload is silent too. Two departures are disclosed: no initial-load suppression (Go's old != nil), and comparison over redacted rows. Both are unobservable in this daemon: the file loads before any watcher can attach, and only one source is ever registered.

Squash ddd2fb8. A report-only change: it rewrote PARITY_AUDIT.json and ports no Go behaviour. Two of its claims were spot-checked against the pin and hold: the AuthKey value printed by printPolicySettings in cmd/tailscale/cli/syspolicy.go, and the CheckTag rewording finding against #482, which #538 later fixed. Its findings are superseded by later fixes where those exist. Nothing in it contradicts upstream.

gate.detail: Run on main at 66ac30e with rustc 1.95.0, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4, TS_RS_EXPERIMENT set. All four stages pass. fmt --check and clippy --all-targets -D warnings: clean. test --all-targets: 42 test binaries, 1267 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored. build --release --bins: finished. The first test run, with this machine's long TMPDIR, failed one test: tailnetd tests::cleanup_refuses_live_socket ('path must be shorter than SUN_LEN', darwin's sun_path limit). That is an environment fault the earlier audit also recorded. With TMPDIR set to a short path, the whole suite passed. The default nightly toolchain here has no clippy, so the gate pinned 1.95.0.

findings.title: --bird-socket refusal line 1 still carries an error: prefix and fork text in Go's %s slot
findings.detail: Go runs log.SetFlags(0) and then log.Fatalf("--bird-socket is not supported on %s", runtime.GOOS), so stderr is exactly one bare line, e.g. `--bird-socket is not supported on linux`. Merged: line 1 is `error: --bird-socket is not supported on this platform or in this build of tailnetd.`, with three explanatory paragraphs below it. A runbook anchored to the start of Go's line, or matching Go's whole line, does not match. Only a substring match on the sentence prefix works, and the doc comment now says so. The PR also cites upstream ref 53a0d659 rather than the ledger pin.

findings.title: --bird-socket is refused on BIRD-capable platforms where Go accepts it (engine-side)
findings.detail: Upstream registers feature/bird through feature/condregister/maybe_bird.go under !ts_omit_bird && (linux || darwin || freebsd || openbsd). On those platforms HookNewBird is set, the guard does not fire, and the path is passed to the engine as wgengine.Config.BIRDSocket. Merged: the flag is refused unconditionally, and tailnetd exits 1 at startup on every platform. The PR says why it did not fix this: the pinned tailscale-rs engine has no BIRD hook. This is engine-side, not something to patch in the daemon.

findings.title: A self-only netmap change sends no self_change frame (engine-side)
findings.detail: Upstream sets Notify.SelfChange from NetMap.SelfNode on every netmap update in setControlClientStatusLocked. A change to only this node therefore reaches every watcher: a key-expiry extension, a MagicDNS rename, new addresses. Merged: self_change rides only the engine's net_map tick, and run_bus emits that only when the peer set changes. A self-only netmap change sends no frame until some later peer change happens. Disclosed and filed as engine ask #46; this needs an engine change, not a daemon workaround.

findings.title: self_change is a five-field projection, not Go's full tailcfg.Node
findings.detail: Upstream: SelfChange is *tailcfg.Node. Its doc says it carries addresses, name, key expiry and capabilities, so consumers like containerboot and kube agents can read self state without the full netmap. Merged: SelfReport carries only stable_id, name, ipv4, ipv6 and key_expiry. Capabilities, tags, node key, primary routes and the rest are missing, so a consumer that reacts to a capability or tag change on self cannot do it from this five-field projection.

findings.title: A config-file opt-in to auto-update fails the config load where Go applies it
findings.detail: Upstream: initPrefsFromConfig and setConfigLocked turn the config into MaskedPrefs and apply them with ApplyEdits and pm.SetPrefs. They never call checkPrefsLocked, so a config-file opt-in (AutoUpdate.Apply true) is applied even where feature.CanAutoUpdate() is false. Merged: Config::apply_to_prefs runs check_auto_update_pref and hard-fails the whole load. On a Homebrew-installed or non-Linux host, tailnetd refuses a config that Go's tailscaled starts with. The PR records this as a deliberate divergence.

findings.title: Auto-update refusal text extends Go's one sentence
findings.detail: Upstream checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked returns exactly `Auto-updates are not supported on this platform.`, or `Auto-update support is disabled in this build` when HasClientUpdate is off. Merged: the refusal text appends a sentence about Hostinfo.AllowsUpdate and a per-ingress remedy, and the Homebrew case replaces Go's wording with its own (`not supported on this installation: ...`).

findings.title: check_prefs runs the exit-node rules before SSH, where Go runs SSH before exit-node
findings.detail: Upstream checkPrefsLocked joins its errors in this order: profile name, SSH, exit node, funnel, auto-update, advertised routes. Merged: the PR reordered only the last two, so the chain runs exit node, exit-node vs advertise, then SSH. A posture that fails both the SSH and exit-node rules reports the two sentences in the opposite order from Go. The PR discloses this.

findings.title: A bad --advertise-tags reaches the operator with an error: prefix on tnet up, not Go's bare line
findings.detail: Upstream: runUp calls prefsFromUpArgs and, on error, fatalf("%s", err). That is log.SetFlags(0) plus log.Fatalf, so stderr is the bare `tag: "foo:bar": tags must start with 'tag:'`, exit 1, in --json mode too. Merged: the daemon returns Go's string, but tnet up prints it as `error: tag: ...` on stderr, and under --json as a JSON {Error} object on stdout. The commit's claim that the refusal is byte-identical to Go's holds only for the daemon string.

findings.title: The two --service refusals still print anyhow's context chain instead of Go's line
findings.detail: Upstream runServeCombined returns errors.New("Error: --service flag is not supported with funnel") and errors.New("Error: --service flag is only compatible with background mode"), and main prints each as one line. Merged: tnet prints `Error: funnel via <socket>`, a blank line, `Caused by:`, then the sentence without Go's own `Error: ` prefix. tests/serve_refusal_stderr_framing.rs pins that shape. The PR leaves these --service refusals as a question.

findings.title: tun-mode refusal is decided before the daemon is asked; Go reaches it after GetServeConfig and status
findings.detail: Upstream: `tun mode is only supported for services` is checked after e.lc.GetServeConfig, getLocalClientStatusWithoutPeers and the `service hosts must be tagged nodes` check. With no daemon reachable, Go prints `error getting serve config: ...` instead. Merged: check_serve_flags refuses --tun without --service before the daemon is asked. Go's order is not reproduced for a command line that fails both ways.

findings.title: The web interrupt arm is installed only after the web-client pref round-trip
findings.detail: Upstream runWeb's first statement is signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt). An interrupt during StatusWithoutPeers, GetPrefs or setRunWebClient(true) cancels the context: the run ends with an error (exit 1), or with exit 0 once the shutdown goroutine runs, and never dies on the signal. Merged: run_web awaits start_tailscaled_web_client before web_interrupt() installs the Ctrl-C handler, so it is armed only after the pref step. A SIGINT during that step still kills tnet with the default disposition (status 130).

findings.title: A CGI serve failure exits 1 where Go logs it and exits 0
findings.detail: Upstream: `if err := cgi.Serve(webServer); err != nil { log.Printf("tailscale.cgi: %v", err) }; return nil`, so a CGI write failure is logged and the run ends successfully. Merged: serve_until_interrupt returns run_web_cgi's error (for example `writing the CGI response to stdout`). tnet then exits 1 with anyhow's `Error: ` rendering.
